newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian dealers expect more unit trusts in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian dealers expect more unit trusts in 1997.

text.p: Nigeria will float more unit trust schemes in 1997 as share prices rise above the reach of individual investors, share analysts said on Friday.
"The time for it has come," Aigboje Higo, chief executive of Counter Trust Securities Ltd, told Reuters.
Unit trusts were first introduced four years ago but many went burst alongside distressed banks in which they invested their funds instead of in shares.
"Contrary to SEC's (securities and exchange commission) regulations they invested in commercial papers and got their fingers burnt," one operator said.
About six schemes are currently in operation and operators are upbeat on a new one due to come on stream next month which they say will infuse new interest in the scheme.
Application for the two billion naira International Banking and Trust Company (IBTC) Nigerian Equity Fund opened early this month and analysts said response has been encouraging.
"Some foreign investors, mainly Nigerians based abroad, are showing interest in the IBTC scheme," Azubuike Okpalaoka of TRW Stockbrokers said.
Higo said the scheme was likely to be fully subscribed. He said two or more new products would also be floated next year.
